subject: Marketplace listing vs private offer — procurement and co-sell implications
messages:
From: Natalie Johnson <natalie.johnson@avahealth.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement question — marketplace listing vs direct contract

Hi Soojin,

Quick question from our procurement team as we're preparing the packaging for the next IT steering committee: would you be able to outline the material procurement impacts we should expect if we buy via AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace (public listing or private offer) versus a direct Redwood enterprise invoice/MSA route?

Specifically:
- How does invoicing cadence work for marketplace private offers vs a Redwood invoice (PO -> net terms)?
- Does listing on marketplace affect co-sell credit timing or revenue share for your partner team?
- Are there any material support/SLA differences or attachment requirements (SOW, security addendum) depending on the route?
- Any tax or reseller involvement we should prep for?

We're trying to give our legal and procurement a short bulleted note for tomorrow. Thanks — even a brief comparison will help.

Best,
Natalie
Natalie Johnson
Head of Procurement, Ava Health
procurement@avahealth.com

From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
To: Natalie Johnson <natalie.johnson@avahealth.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement question — marketplace listing vs direct contract

Thanks for the clear list, Natalie — happy to summarize. High-level guidance below (quick bullets for procurement/legal). Happy to expand any item.

1) Invoicing and PO flow:
- Marketplace (Public listing): customer is billed by the cloud provider; provider issues monthly invoices. If you need Redwood-specific invoice lines, we can provide usage reports but payment is routed through the marketplace.
- Marketplace (Private Offer / Private Pricing): we can configure a Private Offer that appears in your marketplace console; depending on the cloud, payment still flows through the cloud billing (common for AWS private offers). Private Offers can often be mapped to a PO on your side but invoice reconciliation is via the marketplace invoice.
- Direct Redwood invoice (MSA + PO): Redwood issues invoices directly on net terms (e.g., Net 30) under our MSA/Order Form. This is the simplest from an accounts-payable standpoint if your org requires a vendor invoice and Redwood tax ID on the invoice.

2) Co-sell / partner credit implications:
- For AWS/Azure co-sell, Private Offers generally still allow co-sell crediting but the timing and attribution depend on the partner registration process and whether the opportunity is logged in partner portal.
- Public marketplace purchases can make co-sell attribution trickier; we recommend registering the opportunity with our channel team before signing to preserve incentives.

3) SLA, support, and attachments:
- Functionally the product and SLAs are the same regardless of billing route.
- For enterprise support SLAs, a Direct MSA + SOW is usually preferred because it allows us to attach support terms and escalation paths explicitly.
- Marketplace purchases are supported, but if you need custom support SLAs or on-prem onboarding, those are easier covered under a direct contract.

4) Tax/reseller notes:
- Marketplace invoices will carry the cloud provider’s tax handling — this can be preferable or not depending on your tax/legal policies.
- If you need Redwood on the invoice for tax reasons, choose direct invoicing.

Quick recommendation for large regulated buyers: if you need PO/invoice routing, explicit SLAs, and Redwood on legal paperwork, choose Direct MSA + Order Form. If procurement requires a marketplace route for internal controls, a Private Offer is a good compromise — it preserves marketplace ordering while still allowing negotiated pricing.

Attaching a short comparison doc and a pricing scenarios spreadsheet for your review.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Adding a few practical notes on co-sell and timetable:
- Co-sell credit: please loop in your field rep / cloud account team as early as possible. For AWS Private Offers we commonly see credit recognized within the same quarter if opportunity is registered up front.
- Lead times: private offers typically take 3–7 business days to appear in a customer console once created; marketplace listing approvals (public listing) can be longer if vendor attestation is required.
- Discounts and SKU mapping: when we do a private offer we supply SKU mapping for your billing and an invoice reconciliation guide.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with procurement + your cloud reseller (if you use one) to run through the PO and reconciliation steps next week.

— Lauren Bishop

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: Natalie Johnson <natalie.johnson@avahealth.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement question — marketplace listing vs direct contract

Hi Natalie — quick clarifications from partner/marketplace perspective:
- Invoice seller name: for AWS Private Offers the invoice is typically issued by AWS; the seller information can show both the marketplace vendor and AWS depending on region and tax configuration. If you require Redwood on the vendor-issued invoice itself, direct Redwood invoicing is the reliable route.
- SSO/Provisioning: there is no product-level difference — SCIM/SSO integrations and support are identical. Operationally, however, for private offers we provision accounts the same way but we recommend explicit provisioning steps be included in the SOW to avoid handoff delays.
- Healthcare-specific paperwork: BAAs and HIPAA addenda are contractual attachments. We attach them to the MSA/Order Form directly. If you purchase via marketplace and need a BAA, we will still execute a BAA but it’s smoother under a direct MSA because it gives us a direct contractual counterparty rather than routing through the cloud provider.
- Timing: if procurement requires Redwood on the invoice and a PO, plan for direct route. If your finance team can reconcile marketplace invoices against a PO reference, Private Offer works and sometimes speeds procurement sign-off.

If helpful we can draft two short options for your committee: (A) Private Offer flow with checklist (how reconciliation looks, expected invoice fields, timeline), and (B) Direct MSA + Order Form flow (paperwork list + draft PO). Which would help you more for the committee briefing?

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
